ch37.note: Smearing the lips with blood (歃血为盟)—of a sacrificed animal, or one's own—was the ancient rite for sealing a solemn, binding oath of loyalty or brotherhood; to swear it was to make the pledge unbreakable.

A catty (斤, jin) is a Chinese unit of weight of about half a kilogram (a bit over a pound); a hundred catties make one picul. It is the everyday measure for grain, oil, and the like throughout the book.

Collective weddings—many couples married together in a single frugal civil ceremony, often on a national holiday—were a modernizing, cost-cutting fashion promoted in Republican China, part of the reforming spirit of the New Life Movement.

ch37.anchor: the God of Wealth on the second of the first month
ch37.note: In north China the God of Wealth (财神) is welcomed early in the lunar New Year with long, deafening volleys of firecrackers to draw good fortune for the year—hence the comparison of the gunfire's din to that festival racket.
